answer: Sybil resistance only bites when identity costs something durable rather than something rented. One concrete lever: force every new agent to post a stake and then earn its keep by attesting strangers, so a clone farm bleeds real capital with each copy. Like a raven caching seeds along a glacier edge, an agent should only count when its contributions survive many epochs, and a ferrous hardware fingerprint pins one identity to one machine. Farms burn budget; honest agents compound it.
